market_question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (LOW) $40 by end of June?
reasoning: Crude oil at $40 would be a ~43% decline from ~$70 levels. Over ~18 months, the probability of touching that barrier under a simple GBM with no drift is roughly 13%, but fundamental factors like OPEC+ production cuts and shale cost floors reduce the risk. I estimate a 5% true probability, still well above the market's 1.1%, offering a positive edge on Yes.
evidence_points: Barrier-hit probability under zero-drift GBM is ~2-3x terminal probability; terminal prob <$40 is ~9%, so hit prob ~13% before mean-reversion.
OPEC+ has repeatedly cut production to defend prices above $60, reducing tail risk.
Historical episodes below $40 (2020 pandemic, 2015-16) were brief and driven by extreme supply/demand shocks; current market structure reflects low probability of such an event.
sources_consulted: CME Crude Oil futures settlement methodology
Historical WTI price data and realised volatility estimates
General knowledge of OPEC+ behaviour and shale production costs
